record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant epsilon with 0 < epsilon < 2^{-1/2} such that, whenever f and g are in L2_a(D) and |f(z)| ≤ |g(z)| throughout the annulus epsilon < |z| < 1, the Bergman L2 norm inequality ||f||_L2 ≤ ||g||_L2 follows?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1. (Korenblum) There exists an absolute constant epsilon, 0 < epsilon < 2^{-1/2}, such that if f, g ∈ L2_a(D) have |f(z)| ≤ |g(z)| in the annulus epsilon < |z| < 1, then ||f||_L2 ≤ ||g||_L2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Bergman space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ with
$$\|f\|_{L^2}^2 = \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\, dA(z) < \infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<2^{-1/2}$ having the following property? For every pair $f,g\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ such that
$$|f(z)|\le |g(z)| \quad\text{for all } z\text{ with } \varepsilon<|z|<1,$$
one has
$$\|f\|_{L^2} \le \|g\|_{L^2}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The existence question (Korenblum's conjecture for $L^2_a$) was settled affirmatively by W. K. Hayman, who proved that an absolute constant $\varepsilon$ exists (with an explicit small value). Subsequent work by Hinkkanen extended the result to $L^p_a$ for $p\ge 1$ with improved constants, while Schuster, Wang and others further refined the admissible value of $\varepsilon$. The sharp (largest) value of $\varepsilon$ remains unknown, but the existence question posed here is solved. For $0<p<1$, Božin and Karapetrović showed the analogous principle fails.

status_evidence.title: On Korenblum's maximum principle for the Bergman space
status_evidence.snippet: Hayman (1999) proved the existence of such an absolute constant for L^2_a, confirming Korenblum's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The existence part of Korenblum's conjecture for the Bergman space L^2_a was proved by Hayman.

status_evidence.title: On Korenblum's maximum principle
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses improvements of the constant in Korenblum's maximum principle following Hayman's proof.
status_evidence.claim: After Hayman's solution, several authors improved the admissible constant, but sharp value still open.

status_evidence.title: Korenblum's principle for Bergman spaces with radial weights
status_evidence.snippet: Recent extensions of Korenblum's principle to weighted Bergman spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Korenblum's principle is now established in broader settings; the original L^2 conjecture is regarded as solved.
